subject: DPA: data lifecycle termination — acceptance criteria & evidence protocol
messages:
From: Glenmark Systems Ltd. <security@glenmarksys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Glenmark Legal <legal@glenmarksys.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: acceptance criteria for data lifecycle termination and proof of erasure

Hi Vivek —

Advancing through procurement and legal review; two outstanding asks from our side before we can sign the DPA addendum: scope and evidence for final data termination, and the handoff process when jurisdictional custody changes (e.g., we repatriate customer content). Specifically: 

- What constitutes acceptable "proof of erasure" from Redwood (audit log snippet, deletion manifest, chain-of-custody)?
- For backups/snapshots, do you provide a separate deletion manifest and timeline?
- If Glenmark requests onshore handback and later issues a legal hold, what is the rollback / suspension process vs. permanent deletion?
- Are there any geographic carve-outs where Redwood cannot perform certified deletion within the standard window?

Can you share a one-page acceptance checklist we can give to our InfoSec and legal teams? We also need to understand what artifacts (file names/URLs) you can provide when we request evidence.

Thanks — please loop in anyone on your side who should weigh in.

— Priya Desai
Security Program Manager
Glenmark Systems Ltd.
attachments: none

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Glenmark Systems Ltd. <security@glenmarksys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data lifecycle termination — acceptance criteria & evidence protocol

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear list. Summarizing and attaching a short playbook that covers the items you mentioned (redwood-data-lifecycle-playbook-v1.pdf). High level answers below; we can tighten language for the DPA redline after you confirm the artifacts you need.

1) Proof of erasure:
   - Primary artifact: deletion manifest (CSV) with object id, original region, deletion request id, timestamp (ISO8601), and deletion status.
   - Supporting artifact: time-ordered audit log excerpt showing the deletion request and worker acknowledgement. We can provide an HMAC-signed log snippet for non-prod/non-sensitive cases; for production we provide signed manifests and operator attestations.

2) Backups/snapshots:
   - We treat snapshots as separate retention objects. When the primary object is deleted, we mark snapshot TTLs for accelerated expiry if customer requests immediate purge; otherwise standard retention applies. The playbook includes the manifest fields for snapshots.

3) Legal hold / rollback:
   - We maintain a hold flag. If Glenmark requests handback followed by a legal hold, we will suspend destruction and provide a custody receipt. Final deletion requires explicit release of hold by an authorized Glenmark signer.
   - We recommend a mutual-action plan clause: handback window + hold notice timeline (we propose 5 business days to acknowledge hold, 30 days to produce release or escalation).

4) Geographic carve-outs:
   - For a small set of countries with export constraints (list in playbook), certified deletion timelines may include coordination with local partners and legal teams; we commit to a documented timeline in those cases.

Next steps: Karthik will propose DPA wording for the termination & evidence sections and Stephanie will add the operational SLA language (acknowledgement windows, artifacts). Can we schedule a 30-min call to walk through the playbook and confirm the exact audit fields your security team needs?

I attached the playbook and a redline template (proposed-dpa-termination-clause-redline.docx).

Best,
Vivek
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-data-lifecycle-playbook-v1.pdf; proposed-dpa-termination-clause-redline.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Glenmark Systems Ltd. <security@glenmarksys.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data lifecycle termination — acceptance criteria & evidence protocol

Hi Priya / Vivek —

Priya — I drafted suggested DPA language and included two short options in the redline doc (see attachment): 

Option A (operational): Redwood will provide a deletion manifest and a signed audit excerpt within 10 business days of request; snapshots will be scheduled for accelerated expiry within 5 business days unless a legal hold is in place.

Option B (contractual): Redwood will provide deletion manifests and custody receipts within 15 business days; for regions requiring partner coordination the timeline may extend but Redwood will provide status updates every 3 business days.

Inline clarifications I added to avoid ambiguity: 
- "Deletion manifest" must include object id, customer id, source region, request id, UTC timestamp, and operator id.
- "Audit excerpt" must include the minimal log entries that show the lifecycle transition (marked with HMAC and timestamp).
- "Legal hold" shall be an explicit customer instruction with an authorized signer and must include a release or judicial order for permanent deletion to proceed.

Two asks for Glenmark: 
1) Which option (A or B) is preferable for procurement/legal? Option A is tighter operationally; Option B affords more calendar flexibility.
2) Is an HSM-signed manifest mandatory, or is an operator-signed CSV acceptable for now? We can negotiate an SLA upgrade for HSM signatures as a premium compliance add-on.

If you confirm preferred option and artifact format, Stephanie and I will produce final redline language to insert into the DPA addendum.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <security@glenmarksys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Glenmark Legal <legal@glenmarksys.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data lifecycle termination — acceptance criteria & evidence protocol

Vivek / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the playbook — that helped a lot. Glenmark's preference is Option A (tighter operational SLA). For evidence artifacts: an HMAC-signed deletion manifest is sufficient for our InfoSec intake for now; we will escalate to HSM-signed manifests if our auditors require it during SOC cycles.

Two quick follow-ups: 
- Can you provide a one-off sample manifest (sanitized) and a 1-page checklist we can hand to procurement/legal? If possible please include an example audit excerpt showing the timestamped deletion event.
- We'll accept the mutual-action plan language you proposed (5 business day ack; 30 day release/escalation) but Glenmark Legal asked to add a clause that Redwood will notify Glenmark if any jurisdictional carve-out affects the committed timeline prior to the 5-day ack window closing.

If you can drop the sample artifacts into the Drive folder you linked, procurement will prepare the final signature packet. We're happy to do a 30-min call next week to finalize redlines.

Appreciate the collaboration.

— Priya
Security Program Manager
Glenmark Systems Ltd.
attachments: none
